  • parliamentary consent. CO3

questions.question: In what ways did the Whig and Tory factions come to prominence in England? / [CO3] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Whig and Tory factions rose to political prominence during the late 17th century –
  • particularly around the time of the Exclusion Crisis (1679–1681) - Whigs stood for
  • parliamentary supremacy, religious tolerance for Protestant dissenters, and opposition to
  • arbitrary royal power - represent the interests of the commercial, urban, and more
  • progressive classes.
  • Tories - supported the hereditary right of succession, regardless of religion - loyal to the
  • monarchy and the Anglican Church - drew support from the landed gentry - more
  • conservative in their outlook.
  • Two-party system became more formalized with the Glorious Revolution of 1688 and
  • the establishment of constitutional monarchy - Whigs increasingly dominated politics
  • during Queen Anne’s reign and especially in the early 18th century under the leadership
  • of Robert Walpole, often considered Britain’s first Prime Minister.
  • Rivalry between the Whigs and Tories had a profound impact on literature - rise of the
  • Whigs and Tories marked the beginning of organized party politics in England -
  • ideological battles shaped government policy, influenced public opinion, and helped
  • establish the principles of modern parliamentary democracy.
